events.text: The reviewer defect changes the convention decisively: the family value must be `χ(L_t) - χ(O_{C_t})`; a fixed polarization’s Hilbert polynomial has slope `deg H`, not `deg L`. I’ll correct the false blueprint and Lean prose as a bounded source-faithfulness unit, then keep the proof work on the intrinsic Euler-characteristic formulation.

---
name: blueprint-conventions
description: The LaTeX-subset blueprint format and house style — environments, \uses/\lean/\leanok/\mathlibok/\notready, the math-purity rule, and complete (not sketched) proofs.
---

Blueprints are a LaTeX subset (the `leanblueprint` dialect) parsed into the DAG.
Write timeless mathematics — a standalone document, not a project journal.

## Environments

Each declaration is an amsthm-style environment; the recognized ones are
`theorem`, `lemma`, `proposition`, `corollary`, `definition`, `remark`,
`example`, `notation`, `convention`, and `proof`. A statement environment plus
its following `proof` environment form one node's content.

## Per-node macros

- `\label{id}` — a stable id (the DAG node key).
- `\lean{Name}` — the Lean declaration(s) this node formalizes; comma-separate to
  bind several (`\lean{a, b}`) when they jointly formalize the node's statement.
  Each named declaration's signature must match the statement. The mapping need
  not be 1-to-1: a node may name several declarations, and Lean may carry
  auxiliary declarations with no node at all.
- `\uses{a,b}` — dependencies on other nodes' labels; these drive the DAG edges.
  Add an edge instead of re-explaining a dependency in prose. Put `\uses` in the
  statement for definitional deps and in the `proof` for deps used only in the
  proof.
- `\source{slug:page-0001}` — reference anchors for UI popups and audit trails.
  Use page-level ids from `references/<slug>/tex/page-0001.tex` or an equivalent
  manifest entry. Multiple anchors may be comma-separated.
- `\leanok` — the Lean is written and checked. Honest only when its Lean is
  actually checked *and* its dependencies are too. On a `proof`, it means the
  proof is formalized; on a statement, the signature is formalized.
- `\mathlibok` — the declaration is already available in mathlib (no
  formalization needed; treat as a leaf).
- `\notready` — the Lean is **not written yet**: the node's statement stands but
  no declaration formalizes it. Mutually exclusive with `\leanok` (a node is
  never both) — remove `\notready` exactly when you add `\leanok`, i.e. the
  moment its Lean is written and checked. It is a human-facing marker of an
  intentional gap, not a DAG edge.

## House style

- **Pure mathematics only.** No Lean tactics, typeclass/implementation notes, or
  semi-Lean pseudocode. No project history ("since iter N", "our failed route")
  and no conversational filler. Not every Lean helper needs its own node —
  auxiliary or implementation-only declarations can stay unnoded; add a node when
  the result is mathematically meaningful in its own right. In particular, never
  add a `Formalization note` paragraph to blueprint `.tex`: attach implementation
  details, failed approaches, and mechanization caveats to the statement's hgraph
  node with `horizon graph ... add comment` instead.
- **Complete proofs, not sketches.** A node's `proof` is a real, rigorous
  mathematical proof a reader could check — not a hand-wave or a TODO. The way to
  keep it short is to *split*, not to abbreviate: if a proof is long or a node
  grows past a short paragraph, break out the hard step as its own `\uses`-linked
  lemma (down to sentence-sized lemmas if needed) so each node stays small and
  its proof stays complete.
- **One statement's worth per node.** Keep each node to a single mathematical
  statement; don't restate Lean source as prose.
- **Cite by source link, not quote comments.** Add `\source{...}` to the
  relevant node. Keep the retrieved/transcribed page text in `references/` (for
  example `references/<slug>/tex/page-0042.tex`) and let the UI expose it; do not
  paste verbatim source quotes into `% QUOTE` comments inside the blueprint.

   876	\section{The degree map}
   877	\label{sec:pic_degree}
   878	
   879	The disjoint-union structure of \(\Pic_{C/k}\)
   880	(\cref{thm:fga_pic_representability}: a disjoint union of open
   881	quasi-projective \(k\)-subschemes) is indexed by the Hilbert polynomial
   882	\(\Phi \in \mathbb{Q}[\lambda]\) of a representing invertible sheaf
   883	(\cref{def:hilbert_polynomial}). For a smooth proper geometrically
   884	integral curve \(C/k\) of genus \(g\) with a fixed degree-one polarisation
   885	\(\mathcal{O}_C(1)\) on \(C\), the Hilbert polynomial of an invertible
   886	sheaf \(\mathcal{L}\) on \(C\) is, by Riemann--Roch,
   887	\(\Phi_{\mathcal{L}}(n) = n \cdot \deg \mathcal{L} + 1 - g\), so it is
   888	linear in \(n\) with leading coefficient \(\deg \mathcal{L} \in
   889	\mathbb{Z}\). This identifies the connected components of
   890	\(\Pic_{C/k}(\overline k)\) with the integers, the index being the
   891	degree.

1	/-
     2	Copyright (c) 2026 The AlgebraicJacobian authors. All rights reserved.
     3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
     4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
     5	-/
     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.DegreeBaseFieldInvariance
     7	
     8	/-!
     9	# The degree on the relative Picard group over a field (gap G-D5(b), SB-5 descent gadgets)
    10	
    11	For the challenge curve `C : Over (Spec k)` and a field extension `K` of `k`, the relative
    12	Picard group `relPic C (overSpec k K) = CechPic(C_K) ⧸ picFromBase` quotients out the classes
    13	pulled back from `Spec K` — but `Spec K` is a one-point space, so its Čech Picard group is
    14	trivial (`Scheme.CechPic.subsingleton_of_subsingleton`) and `classDeg K` kills `picFromBase`
    15	(`classDeg_eq_zero_of_mem_picFromBase`).  The degree therefore descends to the relative
    16	Picard group:
    17	
    18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicDeg K : Additive (relPic C (overSpec k K)) →+ ℤ`, with the anchor
    19	  `relPicDeg_relPicMk : relPicDeg K (relPicMk C (overSpec k K) L) = classDeg K L`;
    20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicDeg_relPicAlgMap` — **E-iv-alg descended to `relPic`**: the
    21	  relative degree is invariant under restriction along `Spec` of any `k`-algebra map of
    22	  field extensions, `relPicDeg K₂ (relPicAlgMap C φ x) = relPicDeg K₁ x`.
    23	
    24	These are the two descent gadgets of `informal/deg-d5b-worksheet.md` §4 SB-5; the `degAt`
    25	brick (SB-6) consumes `relPicDeg` and `relPicDeg_relPicAlgMap` verbatim — on a field
    26	representative `(K', y)` of an étale-locally-trivial class, the honest degree is
    27	`relPicDeg K' y`, well-defined across representatives by `relPicDeg_relPicAlgMap`.
    28	-/
    29	
    30	set_option autoImplicit false
    31	
    32	universe u
    33	
    34	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
    35	
    36	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    37	
    38	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    39	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    40	
    41	/-! ## `classDeg` kills the classes from the base -/
    42	
    43	/-- **The degree vanishes on classes pulled back from the base field**: `Spec K` is a
    44	one-point space, so its Čech Picard group is trivial and every class of `picFromBase` is
    45	trivial. -/
    46	theorem classDeg_eq_zero_of_mem_picFromBase {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    47	    {L : (C ⊗ overSpec k K).left.CechPic} (hL : L ∈ picFromBase C (overSpec k K)) :
    48	    classDeg K L = 0 := by
    49	  obtain ⟨N, rfl⟩ := (mem_picFromBase_iff C).mp hL
    50	  haveI : Subsingleton (overSpec k K).left :=
    51	    inferInstanceAs (Subsingleton (PrimeSpectrum K))
    52	  rw [Scheme.CechPic.eq_one_of_subsingleton (overSpec k K).left N, map_one, classDeg_one]
    53	
    54	/-! ## The relative degree -/
    55	
    56	/-- **The degree on the relative Picard group over a field** (worksheet SB-5, first descent
    57	gadget): `classDeg K` descends along `relPicMk` to the quotient
    58	`relPic C (overSpec k K) = CechPic(C_K) ⧸ picFromBase`, because the Čech Picard group of the
    59	one-point scheme `Spec K` is trivial.  The `degAt` brick (SB-6) reads the degree of a
    60	field-representative of an étale-locally-trivial class through this homomorphism. -/
    61	noncomputable def relPicDeg (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] :
    62	    Additive (relPic C (overSpec k K)) →+ ℤ :=
    63	  MonoidHom.toAdditiveLeft
    64	    (QuotientGroup.lift (picFromBase C (overSpec k K))
    65	      (AddMonoidHom.toMultiplicativeRight (classDeg K))
    66	      (fun L hL => by
    67	        have h0 : classDeg K L = 0 := classDeg_eq_zero_of_mem_picFromBase hL
    68	        rw [MonoidHom.mem_ker]
    69	        change Multiplicative.ofAdd (classDeg K L) = 1
    70	        rw [h0, ofAdd_zero]))
    71	
    72	/-- **The anchor of the relative degree**: on the class of `L`, the relative degree is
    73	`classDeg K L`. -/
    74	@[simp]
    75	theorem relPicDeg_relPicMk (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    76	    (L : (C ⊗ overSpec k K).left.CechPic) :
    77	    relPicDeg K (relPicMk C (overSpec k K) L) = classDeg K L :=
    78	  rfl
    79	
    80	/-- **E-iv-alg descended to the relative Picard group** (worksheet SB-5, second descent
    81	gadget): the relative degree is invariant under restriction along `Spec` of a `k`-algebra
    82	map `φ : K₁ →ₐ[k] K₂` of field extensions — the degree of a relative Picard class does not
    83	depend on the field over which it is presented. -/
    84	theorem relPicDeg_relPicAlgMap {K₁ K₂ : Type u} [Field K₁] [Algebra k K₁] [Field K₂]
    85	    [Algebra k K₂] (φ : K₁ →ₐ[k] K₂) (x : relPic C (overSpec k K₁)) :
    86	    relPicDeg K₂ (relPicAlgMap C φ x) = relPicDeg K₁ x := by
    87	  induction x using relPic.ind with
    88	  | mk L =>
    89	    have h1 : relPicAlgMap C φ (relPicMk C (overSpec k K₁) L)
    90	        = relPicMk C (overSpec k K₂)
    91	          (Scheme.CechPic.map ((C ◁ Over.overSpecMap φ).left) L) :=
    92	      relPicMap_mk C (Over.overSpecMap φ) L
    93	    rw [h1, relPicDeg_relPicMk, relPicDeg_relPicMk,
    94	      classDeg_cechPicMap_baseFieldTransition C φ L]
    95	
    96	end AlgebraicGeometry

events.text: The cross-project audit exposes the central carrier gap: AJCR’s `relPicDeg` is genuinely signed and field-natural, but it lives on Čech divisor classes, while AJC’s `PicSharp` lives on actual invertible sheaves; the project already documents that no comparison exists on a non-affine curve. I’m therefore testing a direct AJC route: define the fibre value from its own sheaf cohomology as `χ(L_t)-χ(O_{C_t})`, then prove the first invariance lemmas on the actual `LineBundle.OnProduct` carrier.

     6	import Mathlib.Algebra.Homology.DerivedCategory.Ext.EnoughInjectives
     7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.FreePresheafComplex
     8	
     9	/-!
    10	# Form-B absolute cohomology `H^p(U, F) := Ext^p(jShriekOU U, F)` (P5b input)
    11	-/
    12	
    13	universe u
    14	
    15	open CategoryTheory Limits CategoryTheory.Abelian
    16	
    17	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    18	
    19	variable {X : Scheme.{u}}
    20	
    21	/-- The standard `HasExt` structure on `X.Modules`, made a section-local instance so the
    22	`Ext`-based absolute cohomology below resolves it without the slow `HasSmallLocalizedHom`
    23	typeclass search. -/
    24	noncomputable local instance hasExtModules : HasExt.{u + 1, u, u + 1} X.Modules :=
    25	  HasExt.standard _
    26	
    27	/-! ## Project-local Mathlib supplement — Form-B absolute cohomology -/
    28	
    29	noncomputable def jShriekOU (U : TopologicalSpace.Opens X) : X.Modules :=
    30	  (PresheafOfModules.sheafification (𝟙 X.ringCatSheaf.obj)).obj
    31	    ((PresheafOfModules.free X.ringCatSheaf.obj).obj (yoneda.obj U))
    32	
    33	/-- The sheafification adjunction hom-bijection as an `AddEquiv` (additivity holds because
    34	the right adjoint is an additive functor and composition is bilinear). -/
    35	noncomputable def sheafificationHomAddEquiv (U : TopologicalSpace.Opens X) (F : X.Modules) :
    36	    (jShriekOU U ⟶ F) ≃+
    37	      ((PresheafOfModules.free X.ringCatSheaf.obj).obj (yoneda.obj U) ⟶
    38	        (Scheme.Modules.toPresheafOfModules X).obj F) :=
    39	  { (PresheafOfModules.sheafificationAdjunction (𝟙 X.ringCatSheaf.obj)).homEquiv
    40	      ((PresheafOfModules.free X.ringCatSheaf.obj).obj (yoneda.obj U)) F with
    41	    map_add' := by
    42	      intro f g
    43	      haveI : (SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf ⋙
    44	          PresheafOfModules.restrictScalars (𝟙 X.ringCatSheaf.obj)).Additive := inferInstance
    45	      simp only [Equiv.toFun_as_coe, Adjunction.homEquiv_unit]
    46	      erw [Functor.map_add, Preadditive.comp_add]
    47	      rfl }
    48	
    49	noncomputable def jShriekOU_homEquiv (U : TopologicalSpace.Opens X) (F : X.Modules) :
    50	    (jShriekOU U ⟶ F) ≃+
    51	      ((Scheme.Modules.toPresheafOfModules X).obj F).presheaf.obj (Opposite.op U) :=
    52	  (sheafificationHomAddEquiv U F).trans (freeYonedaHomAddEquiv U _)
    53	
    54	/-- **Form-B absolute cohomology** `H^p(U, F) := Ext^p_{O_X}(jShriekOU U, F)`. -/
    55	noncomputable def absoluteCohomology (p : ℕ) (U : TopologicalSpace.Opens X)
    56	    (F : X.Modules) : AddCommGrpCat :=
    57	  AddCommGrpCat.of (Ext (jShriekOU U) F p)
    58	
    59	/-- **`H⁰(U, F) ≅ Γ(U, F)`** as abelian groups: degree-zero `Ext` out of the
    60	corepresenting object `jShriekOU U` recovers the sections of `F` over `U`. This is the
    61	additive corepresentability of global sections specialised to `p = 0`. -/
    62	noncomputable def absoluteCohomologyZeroAddEquiv (U : TopologicalSpace.Opens X)
    63	    (F : X.Modules) :
    64	    Ext (jShriekOU U) F 0 ≃+
    65	      ((Scheme.Modules.toPresheafOfModules X).obj F).presheaf.obj (Opposite.op U) :=
    66	  (AddEquiv.mk' Ext.homEquiv₀ (by
    67	    intro a b
    68	    refine Ext.homEquiv₀.symm.injective ?_
    69	    simp only [Ext.homEquiv₀_symm_apply, Ext.mk₀_add, Ext.mk₀_homEquiv₀_apply])).trans
    70	    (jShriekOU_homEquiv U F)
    71	
    72	/-- **Injective vanishing**: positive-degree absolute cohomology of an injective sheaf of
    73	modules vanishes. Direct from `Ext.eq_zero_of_injective` (the injective object is the
    74	*second* `Ext` argument, so no restriction of the coefficient sheaf is needed). -/
    75	theorem absoluteCohomology_eq_zero_of_injective (n : ℕ) (U : TopologicalSpace.Opens X)
    76	    (I : X.Modules) [Injective I] (e : Ext (jShriekOU U) I (n + 1)) : e = 0 :=
    77	  Ext.eq_zero_of_injective e
    78	
    79	/-- **Covariant `H^p(U,-)` long exact sequence, surjectivity at `H^{n₁}(U, F₁)`.**
    80	Thin wrapper around `Ext.covariant_sequence_exact₁` at fixed first argument
    81	`jShriekOU U`, for a short exact sequence of `O_X`-modules. -/
    82	theorem absoluteCohomology_covariant_exact₁ (U : TopologicalSpace.Opens X)
    83	    {S : ShortComplex X.Modules} (hS : S.ShortExact) {n₁ : ℕ}
    84	    (x₁ : Ext (jShriekOU U) S.X₁ n₁) (hx₁ : x₁.comp (Ext.mk₀ S.f) (add_zero n₁) = 0)
    85	    {n₀ : ℕ} (hn₀ : n₀ + 1 = n₁) :
    86	    ∃ x₃ : Ext (jShriekOU U) S.X₃ n₀, x₃.comp hS.extClass hn₀ = x₁ :=
    87	  Ext.covariant_sequence_exact₁ (jShriekOU U) hS x₁ hx₁ hn₀
    88	
    89	/-- **Covariant `H^p(U,-)` long exact sequence, exactness at `H^n(U, F₂)`.**
    90	Thin wrapper around `Ext.covariant_sequence_exact₂` at fixed first argument
    91	`jShriekOU U`. -/
    92	theorem absoluteCohomology_covariant_exact₂ (U : TopologicalSpace.Opens X)
    93	    {S : ShortComplex X.Modules} (hS : S.ShortExact) {n : ℕ}
    94	    (x₂ : Ext (jShriekOU U) S.X₂ n) (hx₂ : x₂.comp (Ext.mk₀ S.g) (add_zero n) = 0) :
    95	    ∃ x₁ : Ext (jShriekOU U) S.X₁ n, x₁.comp (Ext.mk₀ S.f) (add_zero n) = x₂ :=
    96	  Ext.covariant_sequence_exact₂ (jShriekOU U) hS x₂ hx₂
    97	
    98	/-- **Covariant `H^p(U,-)` long exact sequence, exactness at the connecting map.**
    99	Thin wrapper around `Ext.covariant_sequence_exact₃` at fixed first argument
   100	`jShriekOU U`. -/
   101	theorem absoluteCohomology_covariant_exact₃ (U : TopologicalSpace.Opens X)
   102	    {S : ShortComplex X.Modules} (hS : S.ShortExact) {n₀ : ℕ}
   103	    (x₃ : Ext (jShriekOU U) S.X₃ n₀) {n₁ : ℕ} (hn₁ : n₀ + 1 = n₁)
   104	    (hx₃ : x₃.comp hS.extClass hn₁ = 0) :
   105	    ∃ x₂ : Ext (jShriekOU U) S.X₂ n₀, x₂.comp (Ext.mk₀ S.g) (add_zero n₀) = x₃ :=
   106	  Ext.covariant_sequence_exact₃ (jShriekOU U) hS x₃ hn₁ hx₃
   107	
   108	/-! ## Project-local Mathlib supplement — naturality of `H⁰ ≅ Γ` -/
   109	
   110	/-- **Naturality of `Ext.homEquiv₀` in the second argument.** The degree-zero `Ext`
   111	comparison intertwines composition with the degree-zero Ext class `Ext.mk₀ g` and ordinary
   112	post-composition with `g`. Project-local: Mathlib has the comparison `Ext.homEquiv₀` and the
   113	composite formula `Ext.mk₀_comp_mk₀`, but not this intertwining as a packaged lemma. -/
   114	private lemma homEquiv₀_comp_mk₀ {A B Z : X.Modules} (e : Ext A B 0) (g : B ⟶ Z) :
   115	    Ext.homEquiv₀ (e.comp (Ext.mk₀ g) (add_zero 0)) = Ext.homEquiv₀ e ≫ g := by
   116	  conv_lhs => rw [← Ext.mk₀_homEquiv₀_apply e, Ext.mk₀_comp_mk₀]
   117	  rw [← Ext.homEquiv₀_symm_apply, Equiv.apply_symm_apply]
   118	
   119	/-- **Naturality of `freeYonedaHomEquiv` in the coefficient presheaf.** Post-composition by a
   120	morphism of presheaves of modules `q` corresponds, under the free–Yoneda evaluation bijection,
   121	to applying `q` on sections over `V`. Project-local: the underlying bijection is project-local
   122	(`freeYonedaHomEquiv`), so is its naturality. -/
   123	private lemma freeYonedaHomEquiv_naturality (V : TopologicalSpace.Opens X)
   124	    {F₁ F₂ : X.PresheafOfModules}
   125	    (ψ : (PresheafOfModules.free X.ringCatSheaf.obj).obj (yoneda.obj V) ⟶ F₁) (q : F₁ ⟶ F₂) :
   126	    freeYonedaHomEquiv V F₂ (ψ ≫ q)
   127	      = (ConcreteCategory.hom (q.app (Opposite.op V))) (freeYonedaHomEquiv V F₁ ψ) := by
   128	  rw [freeYonedaHomEquiv_apply, freeYonedaHomEquiv_apply, PresheafOfModules.comp_app,
   129	    ModuleCat.comp_apply]
   130	
   131	/-- **Naturality of `sheafificationHomAddEquiv` in the coefficient sheaf.** This is the
   132	naturality of the sheafification adjunction's hom-bijection in its right (codomain) argument;
   133	the right adjoint is `Scheme.Modules.toPresheafOfModules X` (definitionally the forget–restrict
   134	composite). Project-local because `sheafificationHomAddEquiv` is the project's additive
   135	packaging of that bijection. -/
   136	private lemma sheafificationHomAddEquiv_naturality (U : TopologicalSpace.Opens X)
   137	    {F₁ F₂ : X.Modules} (h : jShriekOU U ⟶ F₁) (g : F₁ ⟶ F₂) :
   138	    sheafificationHomAddEquiv U F₂ (h ≫ g)
   139	      = sheafificationHomAddEquiv U F₁ h ≫ (Scheme.Modules.toPresheafOfModules X).map g :=
   140	  (PresheafOfModules.sheafificationAdjunction (𝟙 X.ringCatSheaf.obj)).homEquiv_naturality_right h g
   141	
   142	/-- **Naturality of `jShriekOU_homEquiv` in the coefficient sheaf.** Composing a map
   143	`jShriekOU U ⟶ F₁` with `g : F₁ ⟶ F₂` corresponds, under corepresentability, to applying `g` on
   144	sections over `U`. Project-local: assembled from the naturality of the two project-local halves
   145	(`sheafificationHomAddEquiv` and `freeYonedaHomEquiv`). -/
   146	private lemma jShriekOU_homEquiv_naturality (U : TopologicalSpace.Opens X)
   147	    {F₁ F₂ : X.Modules} (h : jShriekOU U ⟶ F₁) (g : F₁ ⟶ F₂) :
   148	    jShriekOU_homEquiv U F₂ (h ≫ g)
   149	      = (ConcreteCategory.hom (((Scheme.Modules.toPresheafOfModules X).map g).app (Opposite.op U)))
   150	          (jShriekOU_homEquiv U F₁ h) := by
   151	  change freeYonedaHomEquiv U _ (sheafificationHomAddEquiv U F₂ (h ≫ g)) = _
   152	  rw [sheafificationHomAddEquiv_naturality, freeYonedaHomEquiv_naturality]

    11	/-!
    12	# The P2 cohomology kit: `h⁰`, `h¹`, `χ` on a 2-affine Čech cover
    13	
    14	For a scheme `C` over a base
    15	ring `k` (structure morphism `C.hom : C.left ⟶ Spec k`; in the intended
    16	application `k` is a field, but the carrier layer is stated over any
    17	commutative ring, so the same kit serves noetherian bases), a sheaf of modules
    18	`M : C.left.Modules`, and a bundled 2-affine Mayer–Vietoris cover
    19	`S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare`, this file upgrades the `AddMonoidHom`-level
    20	Čech vocabulary `AffineCoverMVSquare.moduleSectionDiff` /
    21	`AffineCoverMVSquare.moduleH1Cok` (`Picard/RigidPushforward.lean`) to
    22	`k`-linear form and defines the numerical invariants:
    23	
    24	* `Scheme.BaseSections C M U` — the sections `Γ(M, U)` as a `k`-module, the
    25	  `k`-structure being restriction of scalars along the structure ring map
    26	  `k → Γ(C, U)` (`toModuleKSheaf.kToSection`, the same scalar path as the
    27	  sheaf-of-`k`-modules dialect `toModuleKSheaf`, so the two dialects agree on
    28	  the nose for the structure sheaf).  The module-instance path is pinned
    29	  ONCE, on this type synonym: `Module.compHom` along `kToSection C (op U)`.
    30	* `AffineCoverMVSquare.sectionDiffₗ` — the difference-of-restrictions map as
    31	  a `k`-linear map (same underlying function as `moduleSectionDiff`);
    32	* `AffineCoverMVSquare.H0ₗ` (kernel submodule), `AffineCoverMVSquare.H1Cokₗ`
    33	  (cokernel `k`-module, same underlying group as `moduleH1Cok`);
    34	* `AffineCoverMVSquare.h0`, `.h1` (`Module.finrank`s), `.chi := h0 - h1`.
    35	
    36	**Cover discipline.**  All invariants are pinned **on a chosen
    37	cover `S`**.  Cover-independence is deliberately out of scope here:
    38	it is to be discharged Čech-to-Čech (comparing two 2-affine covers through
    39	their common refinement, exactly as `hModuleOneEquivH1Cok_curve` compares
    40	Čech to derived `H¹` through the Mayer–Vietoris `(0,1)`-slice) — **never**
    41	through the `HasCechToHModuleIso` comparison gate, which remains
    42	instance-free.  For `H⁰` cover-independence is already trivial and proved
    43	here (`globalSectionsEquivH0ₗ`: the kernel is the global sections, by the
    44	sheaf condition); for `H¹` of the structure sheaf it is inherited from the
    45	gate-free derived comparison (`hModuleOneEquivH1Cokₗ_unit` below, both sides
    46	being `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)`).
    47	
    48	## The `𝒪_C` base case
    49	
    50	For `M = 𝒪_C` (the rank-one free module `SheafOfModules.unit`) over a field:
    51	
    52	* `unitH1CokₗEquiv` / `hModuleOneEquivH1Cokₗ_unit` — the `X.Modules`-dialect
    53	  Čech `Ȟ¹(S, 𝒪)` agrees with the sheaf-of-`k`-modules dialect and hence,
    54	  gate-free, with the genus carrier `H¹(C, 𝒪_C) = HModule k (toModuleKSheaf C) 1`
    55	  (`hModuleOneEquivH1Cok_curve`, `RiemannRoch/Adelic/GenusUnconditional.lean`)
    56	  — for EVERY field `k` (imperfect included) and every cover `S`;
    57	* `h1_unit_eq_genus` — `h¹(𝒪_C) = genus C` on every cover;
    58	* `h0_unit_eq_one` — `h⁰(𝒪_C) = 1` (sheaf gluing + the unconditional
    59	  field-of-constants theorem `Γ(C, 𝒪_C) ≃ₐ[k] k`,
    60	  `Picard/SectionRingUniversal.lean`);
    61	* `chi_unit_eq_one_sub_genus` — **`χ(𝒪_C) = 1 - g`**.
    62	
    63	## Base-change finiteness transport for `𝒪` (Λ-stability consumers)
    64	
    65	The substrate of `RiemannRoch/CurveBaseChange.lean` makes
    66	`C_κ := Scheme.baseChangeField C κ` an AJC curve over any field extension
    67	`κ/k` by *named instances*, so the general-field statements above apply to
    68	`C_κ` verbatim at base field `κ`.  The named transports are
    69	`module_finite_H0ₗ_unit_baseChangeField`,
    70	`module_finite_H1Cokₗ_unit_baseChangeField`, `h0_unit_baseChangeField_eq_one`
    71	and `h1_unit_baseChangeField_eq_genus`.
    72	
    73	Statement discipline: every statement quantifies over ALL base fields
    74	(no perfectness, no algebraic closedness); everything is cover-parameterized;
    75	no `Prop`-class gate is consumed or instantiated.
    76	-/

    88	/-! ## §1. Sections of a sheaf of modules as modules over the base ring
    89	
    90	The base-ring structure on `Γ(M, U)` comes from the structure morphism
    91	`C.hom : C.left ⟶ Spec k` through the per-open structure ring map
    92	`toModuleKSheaf.kToSection C (op U) : k →+* Γ(C, U)`
    93	(`Cohomology/StructureSheafModuleK/Presheaf.lean`) — the SAME scalar path as
    94	the sheaf-of-`k`-modules dialect `toModuleKSheaf`, which is what makes the
    95	`𝒪_C` comparison below definitional.  The instance path is pinned once, on
    96	the type synonym `BaseSections`. -/
    97	
    98	section BaseSections
    99	
   100	variable {k : Type u} [CommRing k]
   101	
   102	/-- The sections `Γ(M, U)` of a sheaf of modules `M` on a `k`-scheme `C`,
   103	as a module over the base ring `k` (type synonym; the `k`-module instance
   104	below is restriction of scalars along the structure ring map
   105	`k → Γ(C, U)`).  The scheme is carried as an object `C : Over (Spec k)` so
   106	that the structure morphism — hence the `k`-action — is part of the data. -/
   107	@[nolint unusedArguments]
   108	def BaseSections (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (M : C.left.Modules)
   109	    (U : C.left.Opens) : Type u :=
   110	  Γ(M, U)
   111	
   112	noncomputable instance (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (M : C.left.Modules)
   113	    (U : C.left.Opens) : AddCommGroup (BaseSections C M U) :=
   114	  inferInstanceAs (AddCommGroup Γ(M, U))
   115	
   116	/-- The per-open structure ring map `k →+* Γ(C, U)` of a `k`-scheme `C`,
   117	respelled on the scheme-sections notation `Γ(C.left, U)` (so that the
   118	tautological module instance `Module Γ(C.left, U) Γ(M, U)` is keyed
   119	correctly).  Definitional: it IS `toModuleKSheaf.kToSection C (op U)`
   120	(`baseRingMap_eq_kToSection`), the scalar path of the sheaf-of-`k`-modules
   121	dialect. -/
   122	noncomputable def baseRingMap (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (U : C.left.Opens) :
   123	    k →+* Γ(C.left, U) :=
   124	  (toModuleKSheaf.kToSection C (Opposite.op U)).hom
   125	
   126	/-- `baseRingMap` is the structure ring map of the `toModuleKSheaf` dialect. -/
   127	lemma baseRingMap_eq_kToSection (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (U : C.left.Opens) :
   128	    baseRingMap C U = (toModuleKSheaf.kToSection C (Opposite.op U)).hom :=
   129	  rfl
   130	
   131	/-- `baseRingMap` commutes with restriction: restriction of the constant `c`
   132	from `U` to `V ≤ U` is the constant `c` (`toModuleKSheaf.algebraMap_naturality`). -/
   133	lemma baseRingMap_naturality (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) {U V : C.left.Opens}
   134	    (h : V ≤ U) (c : k) :
   135	    (C.left.presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op).hom (baseRingMap C U c) = baseRingMap C V c :=
   136	  toModuleKSheaf.algebraMap_naturality (C := C) ((homOfLE h).op) c
   137	
   138	/-- The pinned `k`-module instance path on sections: restriction of scalars
   139	along the structure ring map `baseRingMap C U : k →+* Γ(C, U)`, acting
   140	through the tautological `Γ(C, U)`-module structure on `Γ(M, U)`. -/
   141	noncomputable instance (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (M : C.left.Modules)
   142	    (U : C.left.Opens) : Module k (BaseSections C M U) :=
   143	  Module.compHom Γ(M, U) (baseRingMap C U)
   144	
   145	/-- Reinterpret an element of `BaseSections C M U` as a raw section of the
   146	abelian presheaf of `M` (the identity function; the definitional bridge
   147	between the `k`-module synonym and the `Γ(C, U)`-module of sections). -/
   148	def BaseSections.val {C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} {M : C.left.Modules}
   149	    {U : C.left.Opens} (m : BaseSections C M U) : Γ(M, U) := m
   150	
   151	/-- The definitional spelling of the `k`-action on `BaseSections`: scalars act
   152	through the structure ring map.  (`rfl`; stated so consumers never unfold the
   153	`Module.compHom` instance by hand.) -/
   154	lemma BaseSections.smul_def (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (M : C.left.Modules)
   155	    (U : C.left.Opens) (c : k) (m : BaseSections C M U) :
   156	    (c • m).val = baseRingMap C U c • m.val :=
   157	  rfl
   158	
   159	/-- The restriction map `Γ(M, U) → Γ(M, V)` (`V ≤ U`) of a sheaf of modules is
   160	`k`-linear for the base-ring structure of `BaseSections`: restriction is
   161	semilinear over the structure-sheaf restriction, and the structure ring maps
   162	are compatible with restriction (`toModuleKSheaf.algebraMap_naturality`). -/
   163	noncomputable def BaseSections.restrictₗ (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
   164	    (M : C.left.Modules) {U V : C.left.Opens} (h : V ≤ U) :
   165	    BaseSections C M U →ₗ[k] BaseSections C M V where
   166	  toFun := (M.presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op).hom
   167	  map_add' := map_add _
   168	  map_smul' c x := by
   169	    change (M.presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op).hom (baseRingMap C U c • BaseSections.val x) =
   170	      baseRingMap C V c • (M.presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op).hom (BaseSections.val x)
   171	    rw [← baseRingMap_naturality C h c]
   172	    exact Modules.map_smul M (homOfLE h) (baseRingMap C U c) (BaseSections.val x)
   173	
   174	@[simp] lemma BaseSections.restrictₗ_apply (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
   175	    (M : C.left.Modules) {U V : C.left.Opens} (h : V ≤ U) (x : BaseSections C M U) :
   176	    BaseSections.restrictₗ C M h x = (M.presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op).hom x :=
   177	  rfl
   178	
   179	end BaseSections
   180	
   181	/-! ## §2. The `k`-linear Čech kit on a 2-affine cover: `H⁰ₗ`, `Ȟ¹ₗ`, `h⁰`, `h¹`, `χ` -/
   182	
   183	section CechKit
   184	
   185	variable {k : Type u} [CommRing k]
   186	variable (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
   187	
   188	/-- **The difference-of-restrictions map, `k`-linear form**: the base-ring
   189	linear upgrade of `AffineCoverMVSquare.moduleSectionDiff`
   190	(`Picard/RigidPushforward.lean`) for a sheaf of modules `M` on a `k`-scheme
   191	`C`:
   192	`Γ(U₁, M) × Γ(U₂, M) →ₗ[k] Γ(U₁ ⊓ U₂, M)`, `(a, b) ↦ a|₁₂ − b|₁₂`.
   193	Same underlying function as `moduleSectionDiff`
   194	(`sectionDiffₗ_coe_moduleSectionDiff`). -/
   195	noncomputable def AffineCoverMVSquare.sectionDiffₗ (S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare)
   196	    (M : C.left.Modules) :
   197	    BaseSections C M S.U₁ × BaseSections C M S.U₂ →ₗ[k]
   198	      BaseSections C M (S.U₁ ⊓ S.U₂) :=
   199	  (BaseSections.restrictₗ C M inf_le_left).comp (LinearMap.fst k _ _) -
   200	    (BaseSections.restrictₗ C M inf_le_right).comp (LinearMap.snd k _ _)
   201	
   202	/-- The value of the `k`-linear difference map. -/
   203	lemma AffineCoverMVSquare.sectionDiffₗ_apply (S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare)
   204	    (M : C.left.Modules) (p : BaseSections C M S.U₁ × BaseSections C M S.U₂) :
   205	    S.sectionDiffₗ C M p =
   206	      (M.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left : S.U₁ ⊓ S.U₂ ≤ S.U₁)).op).hom p.1 -
   207	        (M.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_right : S.U₁ ⊓ S.U₂ ≤ S.U₂)).op).hom p.2 :=
   208	  rfl
   209	
   210	/-- The `k`-linear difference map has the same underlying function as the
   211	`AddMonoidHom`-level `moduleSectionDiff`; this is what transports every
   212	statement about the additive kit to the `k`-linear kit and back. -/
   213	lemma AffineCoverMVSquare.sectionDiffₗ_coe_moduleSectionDiff
   214	    (S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare) (M : C.left.Modules) :
   215	    ⇑(S.sectionDiffₗ C M) = ⇑(S.moduleSectionDiff M) :=
   216	  rfl
   217	
   218	/-- **`H⁰` on the cover, as a submodule**: the kernel of the `k`-linear
   219	difference map — pairs of sections agreeing on the overlap.  By the sheaf
   220	condition this is the global sections (`globalSectionsEquivH0ₗ`), which is
   221	why `h0` is honestly cover-independent already at this wave. -/
   222	noncomputable def AffineCoverMVSquare.H0ₗ (S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare)
   223	    (M : C.left.Modules) :
   224	    Submodule k (BaseSections C M S.U₁ × BaseSections C M S.U₂) :=
   225	  LinearMap.ker (S.sectionDiffₗ C M)
   226	
   227	/-- **The concrete Čech `Ȟ¹` of the cover, as a `k`-module**: the cokernel
   228	`Γ(U₁ ⊓ U₂, M) ⧸ im(sectionDiffₗ)`.  Same underlying abelian group as
   229	`AffineCoverMVSquare.moduleH1Cok` (the ranges of `sectionDiffₗ` and
   230	`moduleSectionDiff` coincide, `sectionDiffₗ_coe_moduleSectionDiff`). -/
   231	noncomputable def AffineCoverMVSquare.H1Cokₗ (S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare)
   232	    (M : C.left.Modules) : Type u :=
   233	  BaseSections C M (S.U₁ ⊓ S.U₂) ⧸ LinearMap.range (S.sectionDiffₗ C M)
   234	
   235	noncomputable instance (S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare) (M : C.left.Modules) :
   236	    AddCommGroup (S.H1Cokₗ C M) :=
   237	  inferInstanceAs (AddCommGroup (_ ⧸ LinearMap.range (S.sectionDiffₗ C M)))
   238	
   239	noncomputable instance (S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare) (M : C.left.Modules) :
   240	    Module k (S.H1Cokₗ C M) :=
   241	  inferInstanceAs (Module k (_ ⧸ LinearMap.range (S.sectionDiffₗ C M)))
   242	
   243	/-- **`h⁰(M)` on the cover `S`**: the `k`-dimension of the kernel of the
   244	difference map (junk value `0` when infinite-dimensional; finiteness for
   245	general coherent `M` is a later P2 wave). -/
   246	noncomputable def AffineCoverMVSquare.h0 (S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare)
   247	    (M : C.left.Modules) : ℕ :=
   248	  Module.finrank k (S.H0ₗ C M)
   249	
   250	/-- **`h¹(M)` on the cover `S`**: the `k`-dimension of the concrete Čech
   251	cokernel (junk value `0` when infinite-dimensional). -/
   252	noncomputable def AffineCoverMVSquare.h1 (S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare)
   253	    (M : C.left.Modules) : ℕ :=
   254	  Module.finrank k (S.H1Cokₗ C M)
   255	
   256	/-- **The Euler characteristic `χ(M) = h⁰(M) − h¹(M)` on the cover `S`.**
   257	It agrees with the sheaf-theoretic `χ` whenever both `h⁰` and `h¹` are finite
   258	and the cover computes them, which for the curves considered here is every
   259	2-affine cover. -/
   260	noncomputable def AffineCoverMVSquare.chi (S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare)
   261	    (M : C.left.Modules) : ℤ :=
   262	  (S.h0 C M : ℤ) - (S.h1 C M : ℤ)
   263	
   264	lemma AffineCoverMVSquare.chi_def (S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare)
   265	    (M : C.left.Modules) :
   266	    S.chi C M = (S.h0 C M : ℤ) - (S.h1 C M : ℤ) :=
   267	  rfl
   268	
   269	end CechKit

   271	/-! ## §3. `H⁰` is the global sections (sheaf gluing on the 2-cover)
   272	
   273	The kernel of the difference map is `Γ(C, M)`: restriction into the pair is
   274	injective (separatedness) and hits every agreeing pair (gluing), both through
   275	the sheaf property of `M.presheaf` on the cover `{U₁, U₂}` of `⊤`.  This is
   276	the trivial half of cover-independence, done at this wave because the `𝒪`
   277	base case needs it. -/
   278	
   279	section Gluing
   280	
   281	variable {k : Type u} [CommRing k]
   282	variable (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
   283	
   284	/-- The pair-of-restrictions map `Γ(M, ⊤) →ₗ[k] Γ(U₁, M) × Γ(U₂, M)`, the
   285	`k`-linear upgrade of `AffineCoverMVSquare.moduleSectionRes`. -/
   286	noncomputable def AffineCoverMVSquare.sectionResₗ (S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare)
   287	    (M : C.left.Modules) :
   288	    BaseSections C M (⊤ : C.left.Opens) →ₗ[k]
   289	      BaseSections C M S.U₁ × BaseSections C M S.U₂ :=
   290	  (BaseSections.restrictₗ C M le_top).prod (BaseSections.restrictₗ C M le_top)
   291	
   292	/-- The pair of restrictions of a global section agrees on the overlap: the
   293	two-term complex property, `k`-linear form. -/
   294	lemma AffineCoverMVSquare.sectionDiffₗ_sectionResₗ (S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare)
   295	    (M : C.left.Modules) (s : BaseSections C M (⊤ : C.left.Opens)) :
   296	    S.sectionDiffₗ C M (S.sectionResₗ C M s) = 0 := by
   297	  have h := congrArg (fun f => f s) (S.moduleSectionDiff_comp_moduleSectionRes M)
   298	  exact h
   299	
   300	/-- The two-element indexed family `{U₁, U₂}` of a 2-affine cover square, used
   301	to feed the Mathlib sheaf-condition API. -/
   302	noncomputable def AffineCoverMVSquare.pairFamily {X : Scheme.{u}}
   303	    (S : X.AffineCoverMVSquare) : ULift.{u} Bool → X.Opens :=
   304	  fun i => bif i.down then S.U₁ else S.U₂
   305	
   306	lemma AffineCoverMVSquare.le_iSup_pairFamily {X : Scheme.{u}}
   307	    (S : X.AffineCoverMVSquare) : (⊤ : X.Opens) ≤ iSup S.pairFamily := by
   308	  rw [← S.cover]
   309	  exact sup_le (le_iSup S.pairFamily ⟨true⟩) (le_iSup S.pairFamily ⟨false⟩)
   310	
   311	/-- **`H⁰ₗ` is the global sections.**  The corestriction of the
   312	pair-of-restrictions map is a `k`-linear equivalence
   313	`Γ(C, M) ≃ₗ[k] H⁰ₗ(S, M)`: injective by separatedness of the sheaf
   314	`M.presheaf`, surjective onto the kernel by the gluing axiom, both on the
   315	2-element cover `{U₁, U₂}` of `⊤`.  In particular `h0` does not depend on
   316	the cover. -/
   317	noncomputable def AffineCoverMVSquare.globalSectionsEquivH0ₗ
   318	    (S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare) (M : C.left.Modules) :
   319	    BaseSections C M (⊤ : C.left.Opens) ≃ₗ[k] S.H0ₗ C M :=
   320	  LinearEquiv.ofBijective
   321	    ((S.sectionResₗ C M).codRestrict (S.H0ₗ C M) fun s =>
   322	      LinearMap.mem_ker.mpr (S.sectionDiffₗ_sectionResₗ C M s))
   323	    (by
   324	      constructor
   325	      · intro s t hst
   326	        have h := Subtype.ext_iff.mp hst
   327	        have h1 : (M.presheaf.map (homOfLE (le_top : S.U₁ ≤ ⊤)).op).hom s =
   328	            (M.presheaf.map (homOfLE (le_top : S.U₁ ≤ ⊤)).op).hom t :=
   329	          congrArg Prod.fst h
   330	        have h2 : (M.presheaf.map (homOfLE (le_top : S.U₂ ≤ ⊤)).op).hom s =
   331	            (M.presheaf.map (homOfLE (le_top : S.U₂ ≤ ⊤)).op).hom t :=
   332	          congrArg Prod.snd h
   333	        refine TopCat.Sheaf.eq_of_locally_eq'
   334	          (⟨M.presheaf, M.isSheaf⟩ : TopCat.Sheaf Ab C.left)
   335	          S.pairFamily ⊤ (fun i => homOfLE le_top) S.le_iSup_pairFamily s t ?_
   336	        rintro ⟨(_ | _)⟩
   337	        · exact h2
   338	        · exact h1
   339	      · rintro ⟨⟨a, b⟩, hab⟩
   340	        have hab' : (M.presheaf.map
   341	              (homOfLE (inf_le_left : S.U₁ ⊓ S.U₂ ≤ S.U₁)).op).hom a =
   342	            (M.presheaf.map
   343	              (homOfLE (inf_le_right : S.U₁ ⊓ S.U₂ ≤ S.U₂)).op).hom b := by
   344	          have := LinearMap.mem_ker.mp hab
   345	          rw [S.sectionDiffₗ_apply C M] at this
   346	          exact sub_eq_zero.mp this
   347	        -- the compatible family indexed by `{U₁, U₂}`
   348	        set sf : ∀ i : ULift.{u} Bool, Γ(M, S.pairFamily i) :=
   349	          fun i => match i with
   350	            | ⟨true⟩ => a
   351	            | ⟨false⟩ => b with hsf
   352	        have hcompat : TopCat.Presheaf.IsCompatible M.presheaf S.pairFamily sf := by
   353	          intro i j
   354	          have key : ∀ {U V W : C.left.Opens} (hUV : W ≤ U ⊓ V)
   355	              (x : Γ(M, U)) (y : Γ(M, V)),
   356	              (M.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left : U ⊓ V ≤ U)).op).hom x =
   357	                (M.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_right : U ⊓ V ≤ V)).op).hom y →
   358	              (M.presheaf.map (homOfLE (hUV.trans inf_le_left)).op).hom x =
   359	                (M.presheaf.map (homOfLE (hUV.trans inf_le_right)).op).hom y := by
   360	            intro U V W hUV x y hxy
   361	            have hx : (M.presheaf.map (homOfLE (hUV.trans inf_le_left)).op).hom x =
   362	                (M.presheaf.map (homOfLE hUV).op).hom
   363	                  ((M.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left : U ⊓ V ≤ U)).op).hom x) := by
   364	              have := M.presheaf.map_comp
   365	                (homOfLE (inf_le_left : U ⊓ V ≤ U)).op (homOfLE hUV).op
   366	              exact (congrArg (fun f => (ConcreteCategory.hom f) x) this).trans rfl
   367	            have hy : (M.presheaf.map (homOfLE (hUV.trans inf_le_right)).op).hom y =
   368	                (M.presheaf.map (homOfLE hUV).op).hom
   369	                  ((M.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_right : U ⊓ V ≤ V)).op).hom y) := by
   370	              have := M.presheaf.map_comp
   371	                (homOfLE (inf_le_right : U ⊓ V ≤ V)).op (homOfLE hUV).op
   372	              exact (congrArg (fun f => (ConcreteCategory.hom f) y) this).trans rfl
   373	            rw [hx, hy, hxy]
   374	          obtain ⟨bi⟩ := i
   375	          obtain ⟨bj⟩ := j
   376	          cases bi <;> cases bj
   377	          · -- (U₂, U₂): both maps agree by proof irrelevance of `≤`
   378	            exact congrArg
   379	              (fun g => (ConcreteCategory.hom (M.presheaf.map (Quiver.Hom.op g))) b)
   380	              (Subsingleton.elim _ _)
   381	          · -- (U₂, U₁): restrict the overlap agreement along `U₂ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₁ ⊓ U₂`
   382	            exact (key (le_inf inf_le_right inf_le_left) a b hab').symm
   383	          · -- (U₁, U₂): the overlap agreement itself
   384	            exact key le_rfl a b hab'
   385	          · -- (U₁, U₁): both maps agree by proof irrelevance of `≤`
   386	            exact congrArg
   387	              (fun g => (ConcreteCategory.hom (M.presheaf.map (Quiver.Hom.op g))) a)
   388	              (Subsingleton.elim _ _)
   389	        obtain ⟨s, hs, -⟩ := TopCat.Sheaf.existsUnique_gluing'
   390	          (⟨M.presheaf, M.isSheaf⟩ : TopCat.Sheaf Ab C.left)
   391	          S.pairFamily ⊤ (fun _ => homOfLE le_top) S.le_iSup_pairFamily sf hcompat
   392	        refine ⟨s, ?_⟩
   393	        apply Subtype.ext
   394	        exact Prod.ext (hs ⟨true⟩) (hs ⟨false⟩))
   395	
   396	end Gluing

   398	/-! ## §4. The `𝒪_C` base case: `h⁰ = 1`, `h¹ = g`, `χ = 1 − g`
   399	
   400	The structure sheaf in the `X.Modules` dialect is the unit module
   401	`SheafOfModules.unit C.left.ringCatSheaf` (the `Picard/SectionGradedRing.lean`
   402	abbreviation `unitModule`, spelled out here to keep the import cone lean).
   403	Its sections are — *definitionally* — the scheme sections `Γ(C.left, U)`, and
   404	the `BaseSections` scalar path (`Module.compHom` along `kToSection`) is
   405	definitionally the `toModuleKSheaf` scalar path, so the two Čech dialects are
   406	compared by identity-function linear equivalences.  Chaining through the
   407	gate-free derived comparison `hModuleOneEquivH1Cok_curve`
   408	(`RiemannRoch/Adelic/GenusUnconditional.lean`) identifies `H1Cokₗ(S, 𝒪)` with
   409	the genus carrier `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` for EVERY field `k` and EVERY cover `S`. -/
   410	
   411	section UnitBaseCase
   412	
   413	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
   414	variable (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
   415	
   416	/-- **Dialect bridge on sections of `𝒪`**: the sections of the unit module
   417	(`X.Modules` dialect) over an open `U` are `k`-linearly the sections of the
   418	structure sheaf of `k`-modules `toModuleKSheaf C` — by the *identity*
   419	function.  Both `k`-scalar paths are restriction of scalars along the same
   420	structure ring map `kToSection C (op U)`, acting by ring multiplication. -/
   421	noncomputable def unitBaseSectionsEquiv (U : C.left.Opens) :
   422	    BaseSections C (SheafOfModules.unit C.left.ringCatSheaf) U ≃ₗ[k]
   423	      (toModuleKSheaf C).obj.obj (Opposite.op U) where
   424	  toFun x := x
   425	  invFun x := x
   426	  map_add' _ _ := rfl
   427	  map_smul' _ _ := rfl
   428	  left_inv _ := rfl
   429	  right_inv _ := rfl
   430	
   431	/-- The `X.Modules`-dialect difference map of `𝒪` intertwines, under the
   432	identity bridges, with the sheaf-of-`k`-modules-dialect difference map
   433	(`AffineCoverMVSquare.sectionDiff`, `RiemannRoch/Adelic/Cokernel.lean`):
   434	both are `(a, b) ↦ a|₁₂ − b|₁₂` through the same restriction functions. -/

      "body": "[persistent] [persistent] REPRESENTABILITY PUSH, 2026-07-29 \u2014 the claim/lane protocol that makes 10 free-objective lanes not collide.\n\nWHY THIS EXISTS. This round replaces prescriptive per-leaf tasks with FIVE lanes per project: one REVIEWER and four PROVERS ranked p1..p4. The provers each pick their own target. That only works if claiming is explicit and public. This item is the claiming mechanism. Read it before your first edit.\n\nTHE FIVE LANES PER PROJECT\n- `review-ajc` / `review-ajcr` \u2014 reviewer. Read-mostly. Finds defects of ROUTE and ORGANISATION, not of individual proofs; may propose refactors and file tasks-as-proposals for the provers. Does not race provers for proof work.\n- `ajc-p1` / `ajcr-p1` \u2014 takes the MOST important open representability item.\n- `-p2`, `-p3`, `-p4` \u2014 2nd, 3rd, 4th most important, where \"important\" is measured against the project's representability headline, not by ease.\n\nCLAIMING \u2014 do this BEFORE you start proving, not after.\n 1. `horizon roadmap list --focus <your project's w4-rep / picrep subtree>` and read the reviewer's open notes.\n 2. Pick your item. Check no other lane owns it: an item with `--owner` set to another lane IS CLAIMED. Do not take it, even if you think you would be faster.\n 3. Claim it: `horizon roadmap set <id> --owner <your-task-id> --status active`. If your target is not yet a roadmap item, `roadmap add` it under the right parent first, then claim it.\n 4. Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body \"CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> \u2014 <one line on what discharging it buys>\"`.\n 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. An item left owned by a dead lane is worse than an unclaimed one.\n\nRANK IS A TIE-BREAK, NOT A FENCE. If p1's item turns out to be blocked on p3's, say so in the inbox and swap \u2014 rank exists so four lanes do not all converge on the same top item, not to stop you working on the right thing. p1 has first refusal on any contested item.\n\nYOU MAY PROPOSE WORK TO THE OTHER LANES. Direct-message with `horizon inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane-id> --body \"\u2026\"`. A good proposal names the declaration, the file, and why it is worth more than what that lane currently holds. You may NOT reassign another lane's claimed item, and you may NOT create new horizon runs or tasks for teams outside your own (`horizon permissions` is false on both counts \u2014 propose to the human instead).\n\nSTANDING BINDING DECISIONS you must not relitigate: `I-0491` (AJC: no rational-point binder on the headline; `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` is FALSE and must be deleted, never proved) and `I-0492` (AJCR: `DivFamZar` widens to arbitrary affine opens; do NOT build the GL_2/Aut(P1) route). Read both.\n\nWHAT COUNTS AS PROGRESS, given the 2026-07-29 audit. That audit found 99 of 101 sampled representability claims refuted: 67 sorry-reachable, 17 VACUOUS, 12 hypothesis-shifted. So the bar is explicit:\n- A discharged obligation must be sorry-free AND its hypotheses must be inhabitable. Before you claim a gate closed, exhibit a witness for every antecedent, or say plainly which antecedent is still undischarged.\n- Do NOT add a class, structure field, or hypothesis whose statement does not mention the object it is supposedly about. `HasDivFunctor` is the cautionary case: its field asserted only that a presheaf category is nonempty, `C` did not occur, and it was advertised as the existence of the relative divisor functor. That is a vacuity, and it survived because nobody read the statement.\n- Do NOT discharge an obligation by projecting the hypothesis you assumed (`choose_spec.1` of your own binder). That is `P \u2192 P`.\n- A green `lake build` is not evidence a statement is non-vacuous. Check imports are current before believing a `lean_multi_attempt` success.\n\nCOMMIT DISCIPLINE. This is ONE shared ledger branch with 10 writers. Another lane's integrate sweep can commit your half-written file before you have measured it once. Write risky proofs as explicit `sorry` first, measure, then fill. Stage explicit files, never `add -A`.",

  1142	  \textit{Source: [Milne], ``Abelian Varieties'' (course notes, 2008),
  1143	  \S III.1, p.~88 (``\(\Pic^0(C)\)\dots\ degree zero''); the verbatim
  1144	  source quote is at \cref{def:divisor_degree_pic}.}
  1145	  Let \(C/k\) be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve of genus
  1146	  \(g\) over a field \(k\), admitting a Picard scheme (run-0008: the Lean
  1147	  statement carries the \texttt{[HasPicScheme C]} hypothesis, supplied
  1148	  under a \(k\)-rational point via \cref{def:has_rational_point}). A
  1149	  \(k\)-point
  1150	  \(\lambda \in \Pic_{C/k}(k)\) lies in the image of the inclusion of
  1151	  the identity component \(\Pic^0_{C/k} \hookrightarrow \Pic_{C/k}\)
  1152	  (\cref{thm:identity_component_open_subgroup} applied to
  1153	  \(G = \Pic_{C/k}\), specialised in \cref{def:pic_zero_subscheme})
  1154	  if and only if the degree
  1155	  \(\deg(\lambda) \in \mathbb{Z}\) of \cref{def:divisor_degree_pic}
  1156	  vanishes. Equivalently,
  1157	  \(\Pic^0_{C/k}(k) = \ker\bigl(\deg : \Pic_{C/k}(k) \to \mathbb{Z}\bigr)\).
  1158	\end{theorem}

  1160	\begin{proof}
  1161	  \uses{thm:pic_zero_is_abelian_variety, thm:identity_component_open_subgroup, def:pic_zero_subscheme, def:divisor_degree_pic}
  1162	  A class
  1163	  \(\lambda \in \Pic_{C/k}(k)\) lies in the connected component of
  1164	  the identity --- i.e.\ in the image of the open immersion
  1165	  \(\Pic^0_{C/k} \hookrightarrow \Pic_{C/k}\)
  1166	  (\cref{thm:identity_component_open_subgroup}, specialised to
  1167	  \(G = \Pic_{C/k}\) in \cref{def:pic_zero_subscheme}) --- precisely when
  1168	  the Hilbert polynomial of a representing invertible sheaf coincides
